title: MorseSmaleDecomposer Coons-error refinement (B4c deferred)
description:
PATCH-26 shipped MorseSmaleDecomposer + D-key viewer toggle but the Coons-error refinement loop got SIGKILL'd (exit 137) during the live D toggle on the skull. The recursive refinement re-runs CoonsReconstructionError.compute on each cell each iteration; depth-4 recursion across 67 cells (one cranium-sized) plus the SCALAR-overlay recompute pushes the JVM past the heap allotted by mvn exec.

The cranium currently shows as 2-3 oversized cells in MORSE_SMALE that aren't Coons-fittable. This ticket re-enables refinement with proper memory accounting:

1. Compute Coons error per cell ONCE per refinement iteration, not on every recurse.
2. Reuse buffers — don't clone label arrays every depth level.
3. Skip cells smaller than some min-faces threshold (already partly there).
4. Possibly: refine in a background thread with a progress log, so UI doesn't block.
5. Ensure the BFS region-grow inside a cell uses a face-id → list-index map per cell instead of scanning all faces every time.

Acceptance: D-toggle to MORSE_SMALE on skull does NOT crash, completes in <10s, cranium subdivides into 4-8 sub-cells, Coons p95 drops near threshold.

Test mesh: voyage_skull_ref.obj (24998 verts).

Plan reference for context: ~/.claude/plans/plan-written-targets-crest-line-swirling-garden.md (PATCH-26 §B4c).
definition-of-done:
1. MorseSmaleDecomposer with refinement runs to completion on the skull without SIGKILL.
2. Decomposition completes in <10s including refinement.
3. Cranium subdivides to 4-8 sub-cells in the live MORSE_SMALE view.
4. Coons p95 drops below 1.5x threshold.
testing-plan:
1. Live viewer D-toggle on skull, time the recompose, ensure no crash.
2. VerifyCoonsError on MorseSmaleDecomposer output, compare against pre-refinement and against SemanticPatchDecomposer.
3. Visual: cranium has multiple sub-cells, no single cell larger than ~10% of mesh area.
